record.paper_title: Some open problems in Banach space theory
record.original_question: If Banach spaces X and Y are uniformly homeomorphic as metric spaces, must they be isomorphic as Banach spaces?

evidence.quote:
(Q.13) Let X Y be two uniformly homeomorphic Banach. spaces. Is. X isomor-
phic to Y ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be (real, infinite-dimensional) Banach spaces. A map $f:X\to Y$ is called a uniform homeomorphism if $f$ is a bijection and both $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are uniformly continuous with respect to the metrics induced by the norms. The spaces $X$ and $Y$ are said to be linearly isomorphic if there exists a bijective bounded linear map $T:X\to Y$ with bounded inverse.

Question: If two Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$ are uniformly homeomorphic as metric spaces, must they necessarily be linearly isomorphic as Banach spaces?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has a negative answer. Ribe (1984) constructed two separable Banach spaces that are uniformly homeomorphic but not linearly isomorphic; in particular, a reflexive Banach space can be uniformly homeomorphic to a non-reflexive one. Subsequent work by Aharoni–Lindenstrauss and others (including more recent examples involving subspaces and quotients of $\ell_p$ and $c_0$) provides further counterexamples.

status_evidence.title: Existence of separable uniformly homeomorphic nonisomorphic Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: There exist two separable Banach spaces which are uniformly homeomorphic but not isomorphic (Ribe, 1984).
status_evidence.claim: Uniform homeomorphism does not imply linear isomorphism.

status_evidence.title: Examples of uniformly homeomorphic Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: For every 1<p≠2<∞ there are two uniformly homeomorphic subspaces (resp. quotients) of ℓp which are not linearly isomorphic.
status_evidence.claim: Many further pairs of uniformly homeomorphic but non-isomorphic Banach spaces exist.

status_evidence.title: An Introduction to the Ribe Program (A. Naor)
status_evidence.snippet: Ribe's example shows that uniform homeomorphism is strictly weaker than linear isomorphism for Banach spaces.
